name: Unitika Ltd.
exchange: Tokyo Stock Exchange (Prime, formerly First Section)
title: Unitika — a polymer chokepoint at a crossroads
subtitle: How a 137-year-old Osaka synthetic-fiber maker is restructuring around technical films, glass fibers, and an unsolved succession question
abstract: Unitika Ltd. (3103.T, Tokyo Stock Exchange) is a 137-year-old Osaka polymer and fiber maker mid-restructuring under supervision of REVIC, the Japanese state-affiliated Regional Economic Vitalization Corporation. The FY3/25 results posted a ¥24.3B net loss driven by a ¥37.9B impairment, but the first nine months of FY3/26 show operating profit up 110% YoY to ¥9.0B and net income flipped to ¥10.6B from a ¥24.4B loss. In April 2025 the board cancelled all Class A and Class B preferred shares and issued Class C preferred to REVIC for ¥20B — handing the restructuring fund 66.76% voting control — while MUFG, Mizuho, and Sumitomo Mitsui Trust forgave up to ¥43B of debt. The new president, Fujii Minoru, is a career engineer who joined Unitika in 1987. The strategic plan shrinks the company from ¥126B revenue to a ¥70B target by FY3/29 by exiting textiles entirely (Seiren, Shikibo, Kawabo, Zuiko, and Boken named as buyers) and concentrating on chip-substrate glass fibers, retort-barrier film, semiconductor release film, and millimeter-wave PCB film via a December 2025 DIC partnership. The stock has traded between ¥127 and ¥3,745 over five years and now sits at ¥1,574 for a market capitalisation of ¥90.75B.
